subject: Private deployment onramp: environment authorization & network certification
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Samira Qureshi <samira@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment onramp: environment authorization & network certification

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for your private deployment. Per our kick-off call, attached is a focused readiness checklist that will help us certify the VPC/on-prem environment and complete the authorization gating. Key asks in the next week:

1) CIDR and routing plan (including any secondary ranges you reserve for sidecars).
2) Public egress IPs or NAT IPs we should allow.
3) KMS/HSM provider details and the contact for key provisioning.
4) Service account that we can use for initial smoke tests (we provided a template attached).
5) Preferred maintenance window and on-call contact for the cutover day.

Deliverables linked in the sheet: network-egress-allowlist.txt, service-account-template.json. We can run a dry smoke test once we have the service account and firewall rules.

Proposed timeline: checklist completion within 5 business days, smoke test within 2 business days after rules are applied.

Ben/Kim — please confirm whether the runbook link I included covers the latest MTU and VPN tuning notes for their infra team.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0184

Attachments: privdeploy-readiness-checklist-v1.xlsx, service-account-template.json
From: Samira Qureshi <samira@stratushealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment onramp: environment authorization & network certification

Jordan —

Appreciate the checklist. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we circulate to infra: 

- We will provide the primary CIDR (10.240.0.0/16) and two /24s reserved for sidecars — do you need the exact route table IDs or just the ranges?
- For egress, we currently NAT through three elastic IPs; I can share them but need to confirm whether Redwood supports IP rotation during rollout.
- KMS: we use HashiCorp Vault (hosted by our security team). Our security ops lead is Rajiv Menon — I am looping him in.
- SSO/IdP: we'll want SAML for the Redwood console admin accounts; is there a specific metadata file you require?
- Maintenance window: we prefer UTC 02:00–05:00 on Saturdays.

Looping Rajiv for infra-level items (routing, MTU, VPN). Open to a quick 30-minute hang if helpful — Rajiv, are you available this afternoon PST?

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Qureshi
Head of Platform Operations, Stratus Health
samira@stratushealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samira Qureshi <samira@stratushealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment onramp: environment authorization & network certification

Samira —

Quick responses inline: 

- CIDR: ranges are fine to start; route table IDs are only necessary if you plan to attach our peering or transit gateway directly to a specific table. If you plan to use a Managed Transit we just need subnet IDs.

- Egress IP rotation: Redwood supports a small window of IP rotation during canary rollouts; we recommend scheduling rotation after the smoke test and before the full cutover. If you need zero-change egress during rollout, we can pin the canary to a static egress IP for the first 48 hours.

- KMS/Vault: the service-account-template uses a temporary key wrapper pattern. For production keys we integrate with Vault via a sealed key protocol. Rajiv, if you can share the Vault mount path and the principal we should expect, we can draft the KMS integration doc.

- SAML metadata: yes — the metadata XML file is required for SSO setup. Kimberly, I put the SAML metadata checklist in the runbook link.

- MTU/VPN: Our experience shows MTU 1400 works reliably for IPsec tunnels to cloud hosts; if you use jumbo frames internally, add a note.

Smoke test plan (short):
  • Provision ephemeral service account using the attached template
  • Apply egress allowlist to the three NAT IPs
  • Run a 5-minute synthetic through the smoke harness (token-level latency + success)
  • Verify KV cache warms and logs are visible in the private console (we'll give you a read-only link)

I'll attach the smoke-runbook link and the one-page run checklist to this thread.

Ben Carter
Senior Onboarding Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@stratusinfra.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Samira Qureshi <samira@stratushealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment onramp: environment authorization & network certification

Thanks — Rajiv here (infra). A few technical notes from our side: 

1) VPN: we'll be terminating an IPsec tunnel into your transit. We need your preferred cipher list and a proposal for rekey timing.
2) MTU: internal fabric supports 9000 but the IPsec path drops; we'll standardize on MTU 1400 on the tunnel interface.
3) Routes: we will announce the tenant prefixes via BGP to the transit peer. Can you confirm support for BGP with AS-PATH preservation?
4) Monitoring: we'll ingest a minimal set of telemetry (ping + /health) into our pager system — what endpoints should we monitor during smoke?

Operational ask: can the smoke test be done this Friday 2028-05-18 at 02:30 UTC (your proposed maintenance window falls at 02:00–05:00 Saturday; we prefer Friday for internal ops coverage).

Also, we request a rollback checklist in-case the canary shows degraded p99 latency; please provide a short runbook snippet we can keep on our side.

Regards,
Rajiv Menon
Infrastructure Lead, Stratus Health
rajiv@stratusinfra.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@stratusinfra.com>, Samira Qureshi <samira@stratushealth.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment onramp: environment authorization & network certification

Rajiv / Samira —

Thanks — Friday 2028-05-18 02:30 UTC works for Redwood. Action items before then: 

- Samira: share NAT IPs and the Vault mount path by EOD tomorrow.
- Rajiv: confirm BGP ASN and preferred pre-shared key length; also include cipher prefs if you have constraints.
- Ben/Kim: prepare the smoke-runbook snippet and the rollback checklist (we'll add the short snippet to the shared Drive link).

Kimberly — can you do the SAML metadata ingestion and verify console admin mapping after Rajiv shares the IdP metadata? If you can sign off on SSO and give a go/no-go by Thursday 2028-05-17 17:00 UTC, we'll lock the window.

I'll attach a one-paragraph rollback procedure in a follow-up after Ben confirms the wording. Looking forward to a smooth smoke.

Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com
